title: GitHub Trending Weekly #27: Remodex, chrome-cdp, GSD 2, TADA, ATLAS, skales, AutoResearchClaw

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: What is up everyone? I'm back. I was restricted from posting for a week and honestly it gave me time to reflect on making content that's not just useful but responsible. So let's make this comeback count. Today we're have 35 trending open-source projects on GitHub. Let's get started.

sections.title: Remodex
paragraphs: Tired of waiting at your desk for your AI coding agent to finish? Meet Remodex. It's an open- source app that lets you control OpenAI codecs straight from your iPhone. Start a massive refactor on your Mac. Grab a coffee and get push notifications when it's done. Run git commands, review code, and snap photos straight into your AI's context window, all from your pocket.

sections.title: app-store-screenshots
paragraphs: Ready to launch your iOS app, but dreading manually cropping screenshots for every single Apple device? You need the App Store screenshots tool. It's a native skill for AI agents like Claude Code that completely automates the pain away. Just tell the AI what your app does and it automatically writes marketing copy, applies 3D device frames, and exports perfectly sized assets.

sections.title: chrome-cdp
paragraphs: Are your AI agents opening fresh browsers where you aren't even logged in? You need Chrome CDP skill. It connects your AI directly to your live Chrome session. Now your agent can read your open tabs and use sites where you are already authenticated like GitHub or Gmail. No bloated frameworks, just a direct websocket connection. No more copying and pasting between your browser and terminal.

sections.title: gstack
paragraphs: The CEO of Y Combinator, Gary Tan, just open sourced his exact personal AI setup. And it's called GStack. It literally turns Claude code into a full virtual tech company. You get distinct AI personas like a CEO, engineering manager, and QA tester. The best part, a conductor agent forces the AI to think strategically before writing a single line of code. Ship software like the head of YC AI agents are completely cut off from email. Claude can't send, cursor can't receive. Key ID agent kit fixes that. 27

sections.title: agent-kit
paragraphs: email tools, one npm install. Works with Claude desktop cursor or any MCP client. Your agent gets a real email address. Free, no signup, no API keys. Check inbox, send reply, forward, search, manage contacts, schedule delivery, set autorely.

sections.title: pi-autoresearch
paragraphs: Shopify's CEO just pulled off an absolute masterclass in AI coding. He gave the PI auto research agent one simple instruction for their massive template engine. Make it faster. The AI autonomously ran over 120 experiments, rewriting and testing the code. The result, the entire engine is now 53% faster and uses 61% less memory. It is literally a senior performance engineer on autopilot.

sections.title: skales
paragraphs: A developer spent two hours installing Docker to run an AI agent, then realized his wife and six-year-old could never do this, so he rebuilt the whole thing. Scales is a native desktop app. Download the XI or DMG, double click, done. It uses almost zero RAM and gives you a literal lizard desktop mascot. It autonomously handles your emails, manages your calendar, and even browses the web.

sections.title: CLI-Anything
paragraphs: Making AI control desktop software has always meant fragile screen clicking or halfbaked APIs. CLI anything fixes this. Pointed at any software source code and it runs a seven-phase automated pipeline that maps guey actions to underlying code and generates a complete CLI wrapper with deterministic JSON output. Add it as a clawed code plugin and your AI can edit videos and control massive creative suites without ever seeing a screen.

sections.title: mcp2cli
paragraphs: Building AI agents with MCP. Injecting massive JSON tool schemas is destroying your context window and your wallet. Enter MCP2 CLI. It instantly converts any MCP server or open API spec into a dynamic CLI. Zero code. Gen. Instead of loading giant schemas up front, your agent just uses list and help flags to discover tools on the fly. Boom. 99% token reduction. Works as a skill for clawed code or any LLM with terminal access.

sections.title: mem9
paragraphs: Mem is a hyperfast plug-and-play memory engine built specifically for AI agents. Instead of wrestling with complex vector databases yourself, Mem handles long-term memory storage and retrieval automatically. Your agents can now proactively remember user preferences, past code rewrites, and project context across multiple sessions.

sections.title: GSD 2
paragraphs: Tired of your AI coding agents losing their minds halfway through a project? You need GSD2. It literally stands for get done. This app completely stops context rot by giving your AI a fresh context window for every single task. Just type /gsd auto and walk away. It autonomously plans, codes, and commits until your milestone is complete. Zero babysitting required from the incredible team at Humeai. Tata stands for toneaware data assistant. If

sections.title: TADA
paragraphs: you are building voice AI, standard texttospech sounds robotic and dead. Tata is a framework that natively injects emotional intelligence into your AI. It analyzes the context of the conversation and generates highly expressive, emotionally resonant audio responses. It literally gives your AI empathy.

sections.title: ATLAS
paragraphs: Carpathy's auto research loop but for financial markets. Atlas runs 25 AI agents across four layers. Macro, sector desks, super investors, and a final decision layer. They debate markets daily. Every recommendation scored against real outcomes. Worst performing agent prompt gets rewritten. Runs five trading days. Sharp ratio checked. Improve and it commits. Fail and it reverts.

sections.title: OpenSquirrel
paragraphs: If you constantly jump between clawed code, codeex, cursor, and open code, their motto nails it. If you're going to be squirrely, you might as well optimize for it. Open Squirrel is a blazingly fast native Rust control plane that runs all your favorite AI coding agents side by side in one unified interface. Stop tabbing around and losing focus.

sections.title: temm1e
paragraphs: T1E is an immortal AI sidekick built in Rust that lives forever on your server using just 15 megabytes of RAM. But the crazy part is its lambda memory. It literally mimics a human brain. Old memories fade into compressed hashes to save space, but it can perfectly recall any original detail with 95% accuracy. Hook it straight to your Discord or Telegram.

sections.title: AutoKernel
paragraphs: Building AI models and tired of staring at GPU profilers? Autokernel does it for you. Inspired by Carpathy's auto research, it brings autonomous AI agents to GPU kernel optimization. Pointed at any PyTorch model, go to sleep and wake up to optimize Triton kernels. It automatically profiles your model, then lets an AI agent rewrite and verify new kernels in an endless loop. Over 300 experiments overnight, keeping the fast code and reverting failures.

sections.title: AutoResearchClaw
paragraphs: Want to turn a single idea into a conference ready academic paper? Meet Auto Research Claw. It is a fully autonomous research pipeline. Just type a topic into OpenClaw and it handles everything with zero human intervention. It gathers real literature, kills fake citations, writes and runs the experiment code, and even conducts its own multi-agent peer review, and outputs a compile ready latex document.

sections.title: Mouser
paragraphs: Logitech Options Plus uses 200 megabytes of RAM to remap six buttons and phones home with telemetry every note the entire HID Plus 2.0 protocol and built mouser. 5 megabytes, zero cloud, zero spyware. Per app profiles, 22 built-in actions, DPI adjustment on the fly, full gesture button support via three- tier detection system.

sections.title: Founders Kit
paragraphs: Building a startup is insanely hard, but finding the right tools shouldn't be. You need to check out Founders Kit. It's an absolute gold mine for anyone launching a side hustle or SAS. This massive directory is packed with UI kits, pitch deck examples, angel investor lists, and links to score thousands in free cloud credits. Whether you're a solo dev or an entrepreneur, bookmark this repo right now to save hundreds of hours of research.

sections.title: slides-grab
paragraphs: Using clawed code to generate presentations is great until you have to fix tiny layout bugs with text prompts. It's an absolute nightmare. You need slides grab. Just drag a box over the broken part of your slide. It instantly grabs the exact XP path and a screenshot, feeding it directly to your AI. Claude knows exactly what element to fix, completely eliminating frustrating CSS prompts.

sections.title: Tome
paragraphs: Want beautiful enterprisegrade documentation without Milifi's price tag? Tome is an open-source docs platform where you write markdown and get a stunning fully customizable site with search, dark mode, and API components. self-hosted for free. It actually monitors your code, uses AI to analyze git diffs, and automatically generates pull requests to update your docs whenever you push new code.

sections.title: ghostwright
paragraphs: Sick of slow AI agents guessing where to click? You need Goto. It's a native Mac framework that directly reads your accessibility tree to perfectly understand every app and button on your screen. But the craziest part, it learns by watching. Just say, "Watch me do a task once and it builds a replayable recipe." A fast local model can then run it forever.

sections.title: Animated Icons
paragraphs: Sick of paying for animated icons or using bloated JavaScript libraries? This developer got so annoyed he used clawed code over the weekend to build over 3,000 of them. It takes popular icons like Lucid and adds flawless CSSonly hover animations. arrows sweep status icons pulse and it outputs straight to react view or spvelt with absolutely zero JS required.

sections.title: MetaClaw
paragraphs: Metaclaw from UNC Chapel Hill tagline says it all. Just talk to your agent. It learns and evolves. Just talk normally and it uses online reinforcement learning to extract new skills in the background. If your agent fails a task, Metaclaw instantly analyzes it and injects a fix so it never makes the exact same mistake twice. Agent fails a task, Metaclaw analyzes it and injects it so it never makes the same mistake twice.

sections.title: Skir
paragraphs: Building microservices and sick of wrestling with protocol buffers? Skiar builds itself as like protocol buffers but better. Just define your schema once and it instantly autogenerates type-S safe code for TypeScript, Python, Java, and C++. It handles all serialization automatically and guarantees you never accidentally break backward compatibility. It's literally TRPC for every single language in your stack.

sections.title: Understand Anything
paragraphs: Dropped into a massive undocumented codebase and feel completely lost. You need understand anything by lum 1104. It uses specialized clawed code skills to instantly turn any giant codebase into an interactive knowledge graph. Instead of manually untangling spaghetti code, you can visually explore relationships and just ask plain English questions about how different components connect.

sections.title: lossless-claw
paragraphs: Building AI agents with OpenClaw but hating the context limits. Stop letting your agents delete old messages. Meet lossless claw from Martian engineering. Instead of throwing data away, it saves every message to a local database and condenses it. If your AI needs a detail from last week, it perfectly recalls the exact original text. Real world compression ratios of 25 to1. Your agent never forgets.

sections.title: Startup Domain Search
paragraphs: Have a brilliant startup idea, but every good domain is taken. You need domain searcher-app. It's a free AI powered domain generator that runs entirely in your browser. Just type in your idea and it instantly finds 60 available domains and actually scores them on brandability and memorability. It's 100% private with zero servers so your million-doll idea stays safe. Stop giving AI agents your raw API keys.

sections.title: OneCLI
paragraphs: One mistake and they could leak your production secrets. You need one CLI. It's an open source vault and proxy that gives your AI a dummy placeholder, then seamlessly swaps in the real key in the background. Your agent literally never touches the actual secret. It runs entirely local and even has human in the loop approvals.

sections.title: OpenJarvis
paragraphs: Is your personal AI actually personal if it sends all your data to the cloud? Meet Open Jarvis. It's a groundbreaking framework from Stanford built specifically for local first AI agents. It connects directly to Olama, so your AI runs completely natively on your own hardware. Let it triage your emails, read your private folders, and manage 26 different messaging channels. Your data never leaves your machine.

sections.title: Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep
paragraphs: What if you could outsource tedious research to your AI while you sleep? AutoClaw Code Research in Sleep does exactly that. It's an automation layer for clawed code that lets you queue up deep dive research missions, handles iterative prompts, navigates complex documentation, and manages longunning loops autonomously. Set the objective, go to bed, wake up to a completed research report.

sections.title: OpenMAIC
paragraphs: Want to learn something? Quantum mechanics, a board game, a research paper? Just describe it. OpenMake builds you an entire AI classroom. Slides, quizzes, interactive simulations, project-based learning. AI teachers lecture, AI classmates discuss, they draw equations and diagrams on a whiteboard in real time. You can jump in, ask questions, get called on, export as PowerPoint or interactive HTML.

sections.title: Agent Safehouse
paragraphs: If you're using AI coding agents, there's this reality where they can technically access your entire computer like SSH keys, API tokens, everything. Agent Safehouse locks them into just your project folder using Mac sandbox feature. One script, no Docker, no VMs. The AI can still code. It just can't accidentally wander into your sensitive files. It's basically a leash for your AI agent.

sections.title: nah
paragraphs: Letting code loose on your codebase? Stop right now. One bad hallucination could accidentally nuke your files or expose your private keys. Basic permissions just don't scale. You need the NA tool. It's a brilliant safety guard that intercepts every single AI command in milliseconds before it runs. It automatically detects dangerous actions and smartly blocks or asks for permission.

sections.title: Claude Autoresearch
paragraphs: Want Andre Karpathy's autonomous AI workflow for your own code? You need this new clawed code skill by Udit Winka. It endlessly loops while you sleep, making changes, running tests, and keeping the code only if your metrics improve. Use it to automatically shrink bundle sizes, boost SEO scores, or even run security audits overnight. A tireless AI developer optimizing your project while you sleep.
